newsitem.title: TURKEY: Aid group says Turkey blocking entry to N. Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Aid group says Turkey blocking entry to N. Iraq.

text.p: The British-based Save the Children Fund charity said on Monday Turkish authorities were blocking the movement of aid workers into northern Iraq, jeopardising humanitarian operations there.
A spokesman for Save the Children said the Turkish foreign ministry had not allowed aid workers to cross into Iraq from Turkey since August.
"No fresh permission has been granted since August. Staff have not been able to return to Iraq via Turkey since mid-September," spokesman Parm Unia told Reuters by telephone.
A Turkish Foreign Ministry spokesman said restrictions were being imposed because of concerns about the activities of some aid groups.

"Some of these organisations have been found to be engaged in activities outside of the remit for which they were originally given permission, for that reason restrictions have been imposed," spokesman Sermet Atacanli told Reuters.
Unia said Save the Children staff had crossed regularly from Turkey into northern Iraq since aid operations began there after the Gulf War in 1991.
"Other members of our staff are having to run the operation from a distance, which is detrimental to the programme we are trying to run," he said.
Turkey has in the past said the presence of aid groups benefited Turkish Kurd rebels based in northern Iraq.
